messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> service: redis-cache-high-conns, severity: P1. Page sent to #eng-oncall and oncall rotation.

pagerduty: Incident created: INC-2026-0842. Trigger: redis.maxclients breached on prod-redis-01.

maya (oncall): acked via PD. I'm on it, pulling metrics now. :eyes:

maya (oncall): quick summary: p95 cache latency ~1.1s, error spikes 5xx ~2.8%, redis clients at 99.9% of maxclients (maxclients=10000). Looks like a client flood from api-gateway.

omar: thanks. Any impact to user-facing flows?

maya (oncall): yes — search/autocomplete and embeddings reads show increased latency and occasional timeouts. ~10% of requests degraded. CS already flagged two customers.

opsbot: runbook link -> https://runbooks.redwood.internal/redis-maxclients-flood

sasha: can we short-circuit by enabling client-side throttling at the gateway? We have a quick rule to 429 noisy keys.

maya (oncall): good idea. I'm going to add a temporary rate-limit rule on api-gateway to throttle large-volume api-keys. Command: 
```
# add rule to apigw
apigwctl rate-limit create --key-prefix "sdk:bulk-" --limit 50/s --burst 200 --reason "emergency throttle"
```

alex: also checking pgbouncer. If connection churn is high, pgbouncer could be saturating. Running: `kubectl exec -it pgbouncer-0 -- psql -c "SHOW POOLS;"`

maya (oncall): opsbot, run redis-cli info clients on prod-redis-01 and paste output.

opsbot: ```
# prod-redis-01 clients
connected_clients: 9987
blocked_clients: 12
client_recent_max_input_buffer: 0
client_longest_output_list: 0
```

maya (oncall): confirmed near limit. Plan: 1) enforce gateway throttle to reduce new connections 2) rotate read traffic to read-replica pool 3) temporarily bump maxclients on redis host if safe 4) prepare to spin extra read-only replica if traffic doesn't drop.

omar: bumping maxclients is risky but ok as short term. Sasha/Chiara can you confirm OS ulimit and memory headroom?

chiara: checking now. Redis host mem at 72% used, ulimit for redis process is 11000. We can raise to 14000 for 30m, roll back after.

sasha: gateway rule is in, starting to see drop in new connections after ~60s. P95 latency down to 780ms.

maya (oncall): applying temporary sysctl/ulimit bump: `sudo systemctl set-property redis@prod-redis-01.service TasksMax=20000` and `ulimit -n 14000` (applied via automation). Opsbot, execute config change?

opsbot: patching systemd property and restarting redis gracefully (rolling). Watch logs: `journalctl -u redis@prod-redis-01 -f`

alex: pgbouncer pools looked fine. Few connection spikes but pgbouncer adhered to pool sizes. No leaks.

maya (oncall): after ulimit bump and gateway throttle, connected_clients=6200, blocked_clients=1. Errors down to 0.7% and p95 ~320ms. Looks stable for now.

pagerduty: Automatic escalation suppressed — incident acknowledged by maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): I'm going to monitor for 30m, then hand off to omar for followup and postmortem. Omar if you take the handoff in 30?

omar: taking handoff at +30. Will open follow-up ticket to review client patterns and implement permanent mitigation: client-side backoff guidance + API key rate-limiting per-customer.

chiara: will record the temporary ulimit change and plan a runbook update to include pre-approved short-term maxclients bump steps.

sasha: recommend creating a metric alert for connection-rate (new connections / sec) to catch flood earlier. I'll add to prometheus rules.

maya (oncall): customer impact note for postmortem: ~12% of search reads experienced >500ms latency window for 18m; 3 customers reported degradation. No data loss. Root cause likely a misbehaving SDK client hit pattern.

opsbot: incident annotated: {"impact":"search latency","customers_affected":"3","start":"1749003456","mitigation":"gateway throttle, ulimit bump","status":"stabilized"}

maya (oncall): closing PD incident to maintenance mode. leaving thread for RCA and action items. :white_check_mark:

omar: assigning follow-up tickets: TASK-4123 (RCA), TASK-4124 (Gateway rate-limiting defaults), TASK-4125 (Prometheus conn-rate rule).

sasha: thanks team. Good quick response. We'll do retro and include mitigation automation to avoid manual ulimit bumps next time.

maya (oncall): handoff to @omar complete. If anything pops up ping me.

omar: acknowledged. Handoff notes saved to INC-2026-0842.
